message.content: You are an expert engineer helping the user design a web app.
Hi! I want to start scoping the project today.
Sure, happy to help. What do you want to think through first?
Let's start with the data layer. I'm choosing between MongoDB and PostgreSQL.
For relational data with ACID requirements, I lean toward PostgreSQL. JSONB columns cover most schema-flexibility cases that drive teams to Mongo.
Ack. So Mongo for unstructured stuff, Postgres for everything else?
Honestly with JSONB columns Postgres handles the unstructured cases well enough. Single store keeps ops simpler.
Right, you've sold me. We'll use PostgreSQL for the primary store going forward. Single database, no Mongo.
Solid choice. We can revisit if we hit a write-throughput ceiling, but PostgreSQL is the right starting point.
Hit a bug in staging today. The issue was a missing CORS header.
Yeah, redirected responses lose CORS headers unless you re-add them on the redirect target. Easy fix in the middleware.
While we're scoping — let me state a hard requirement I forgot: the budget should not exceed $50K for the whole project. That cap is firm.
Noted: $50K hard cap. We'll plan around managed-service costs and avoid premium tiers.
For ops, the auth service is going to run on port 8443 inside the mesh. JWKS exposed at /.well-known/jwks.json.
Good — port 8443 is conventional for mTLS-fronted services. JWKS path matches RFC 8615.
Same problem in production now. The issue was a missing CORS header.
Confirms the hypothesis — prod middleware is missing the same header. Let's standardize CORS handling across environments.
Random check: can you list a few cache strategies for read-heavy endpoints?
Sure — read-through (most common), write-through (consistency), write-behind (best perf, eventual consistency), or refresh-ahead. Pick based on staleness tolerance.
Cool, I'll think about it. Talk later.
Sounds good — circle back when you're ready.
Came back today on user-service. The issue was a missing CORS header.
Same root cause then. Let's land the middleware fix today and call it done.
Quick aside — should our retry logic use exponential backoff or fixed intervals?
Exponential backoff with jitter — avoids thundering herd, bounded by a max delay.
Got it. Give me a one-line on observability for the API tier.
Structured logs (JSON), RED metrics on every endpoint, distributed tracing on every request. Wire all three to OTLP and ship to your collector.
Helpful. One more: any pattern for feature flags?
Yes — keep flags decoupled from config (they should be runtime-toggleable), and use a flag store that supports targeting rules and gradual rollouts.
Last thing — order-service hit it this morning. The issue was a missing CORS header.
Understood — let's add a CI check that asserts the header on every redirect response. Fixing it once globally is cheaper than chasing per-service.
